# FDG9081

> DO NOT declare any overloads of `DisposeAsync()`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4.4 IAsyncDisposable.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9081
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Remove the DisposeAsync overload '{0}'; declare only DisposeAsync()

FDG9081 reports a method named DisposeAsync, of any accessibility, static and extension methods included, that has parameters or is generic, such as DisposeAsync(CancellationToken). Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, as for FDG9067. Removing or renaming a public method changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Synchronous `Dispose` recommends the Basic Dispose Pattern (section 9.4.1), deferring `Dispose()` to `Dispose(disposing: true)`, so as to allow the unification of cleanup code between `Dispose()` and any potential finalizer on the type. Since a finalizer is always executed in a synchronous context, it should only ever call the synchronous `Dispose` variant.
